What was assessed: Source and selection of participants; retrospective recruitment; handling of exclusions and of records that could not be linked
Basis: Three cohorts drawn from routine clinical registries; eligibility and exclusion criteria are stated in Section 2.1; the derivation exclusions (45 for image quality, 38 for incomplete records, 54 for previous revascularisation) are enumerated in Figure 1, and the external and contemporary cohorts were extracted as complete consecutive series already meeting the same criteria, with no additional exclusions (Section 2.1); no case-control or outcome-based sampling; the geographical cohort contributed no data to development.

What was assessed: Definition and availability of predictors; timing relative to the outcome; standardisation of measurement across sites; handling of missing data
Basis: The 19 candidate variables were fixed in advance and are recorded before the reference standard is known; no predictor is derived from the outcome, and the outcome term was used only to match records between registries in Section 2.1, never to define a predictor; median imputation was fitted inside the training fold only (Section 2.3). The domain is judged unclear, and applicability with it, because laboratory analyses used the routine platform of each hospital with no central core laboratory and platform identifiers were not retrieved (Section 2.3), and because the univariable discrimination of plasma fibrinogen differed sharply between hospitals and periods (Table S8, panels B and C). Predictor measurement was therefore not demonstrably standardised across the sites to which the model is transferred.

What was assessed: Definition and ascertainment of the outcome; blinding of the outcome assessors
Basis: The outcome is anatomical obstruction on CCTA categorised as CAD-RADS 3-5 (against 0-2), taken from the signed clinical report; it is a standardised reporting system and the category is a recorded field, so the outcome is reconstructed exactly. Risk of bias is judged unclear because the report was not read blind to the clinical and laboratory findings that are the model's predictors (Section 2.2), there was no central adjudication and no reader-level information, and the data set retained neither the CAD-RADS grades nor a reader identifier (Section 4.4). Applicability is judged unclear on a separate ground: the recorded outcome is anatomical obstruction rather than haemodynamic significance, and no functional reference standard (fractional flow reserve, CT perfusion or stress imaging) was available, so the correspondence between the outcome and the disease that drives downstream management in the intended population cannot be established (Section 4.4).

What was assessed: Sample size; overfitting and shrinkage; calibration and discrimination; algorithmic tuning; evaluation of performance
Basis: The derivation cohort is slightly below the Riley sample size for a shrinkage factor of 0.9 (442 patients with 208 events against 470 with 222; a shortfall of about 6%) and no shrinkage correction was applied to the frozen model, so internal estimates are mildly optimistic (Section 4.4). Hyperparameters were tuned on the whole development pool before the cross-validated estimate was computed, and nested tuning was run only as a sensitivity analysis (Table S11, panel A); the external estimates are not affected by either choice, because nothing is fitted on the geographical cohort. Applicability is not assessed for the analysis domain under PROBAST+AI. The additional applicability question 4.10 is reported in panel B for completeness and does not enter the judgement for this domain.

Risk of bias: participants low, predictors unclear, outcome unclear, analysis high; the overall judgement is driven by the analysis domain. Overall applicability is judged unclear rather than low on two grounds: the recorded outcome is anatomical obstruction rather than a functional reference standard, and predictor standardisation across hospitals could not be demonstrated (Table S8, panels B and C). The participants domain is judged low because all three cohorts were drawn from the same population of patients referred for CCTA that the model is intended for, so the referral setting is not in itself a reason to qualify applicability (Section 4.4). The case-mix differences behind these limits are documented in Section 3.1 and Table S3.
